items.title: In the first paragraph the writer makes the point that blind people
options: may be interested in studying art.
can draw outlines of different objects and surfaces.
can recognise conventions such as perspective.

items.title: The writer was surprised because the blind woman
options: drew a circle on her own initiative.
did not understand what a wheel looked like.
was the first person to use lines of motion.

items.title: From the experiment described in Part 1, the writer found that the blind subjects
options: had good understanding of symbols representing movement.
could control the movement of wheels very accurately.
worked together well as a group in solving problems.
got better results than the sighted undergraduates.

items: In the experiment described in Part 2, a set of word <input> was used to investigate whether blind and sighted people perceived the symbolism in abstract <input> in the same way. Subjects were asked which word fitted best with a circle and which with a square. From the <input> volunteers, everyone thought a circle fitted 'soft' while a square fitted 'hard'. However, only 51% of the <input> volunteers assigned a circle to <input>. When the test was later repeated with <input> volunteers, it was found that they made <input> choices.

items.title: Which of the following statements best summarises the writer's general conclusion?
options: The blind represent some aspects of reality differently from sighted people.
The blind comprehend visual metaphors in similar ways to sighted people.
The blind may create unusual and effective symbols to represent reality.
The blind may be successful artists if given the right training.
